end.summary:
Practised levels of organisation in humans and plants.
Ordered cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism.
Identified heart, liver, stomach and intestines as organs; digestive and circulatory systems as organ systems.
Explained that smaller parts combine to form larger levels and that organs in a system work together.
Teach-back on interdependence of parts at one level was not passed.
end.parentNote: Yash practised giving examples and ordering cell, tissue, organ, organ system and organism. They used the method of checking whether one part or several organs were involved, which helped correct the mix-up between an organ and an organ system during the lesson. They also explained that smaller parts combine to form larger levels, but needed more support to explain how parts at one level depend on one another. At home, ask them to choose one system and complete: “Its organs depend on each other because…”
